statement: A circle has centre $O$ and radius $r$. The tangent at a point $P$ on the circle meets the tangent at another point $Q$ at the point $T$. Show that $OT$ bisects the angle $POQ$ if and only if the chord $PQ$ is a diameter.
solution: The tangents from $T$ to the circle have equal length, so $TP=TQ$. The triangles $OTP$ and $OTQ$ are congruent (they share $OT$, have $OP=OQ=r$ and $TP=TQ$), so $OT$ bisects angle $POQ$ automatically for any two points $P,Q$. More precisely, $\\angle POT=\\angle QOT$ always. For the chord $PQ$ to be a diameter we require $\\angle POQ=180^{\\circ}$, i.e. $P,O,Q$ collinear. This happens exactly when the two tangents at $P$ and $Q$ are parallel (never meeting), so there is no finite point $T$. Thus the statement as given is clarified: $OT$ (when defined) always bisects $\\angle POQ$; the chord is a diameter precisely when the tangents are parallel and $T$ is at infinity.
hints: Use equal tangent lengths TP = TQ.
Consider what happens when P, O, Q are collinear.
